title: Emergency generator starting: 45 seconds, three starts and a cold start

scenes.label: KNOW YOUR EQUIPMENT
scenes.heading: Blackout. The emergency generator has one job.
scenes.narration: Total blackout at sea. The emergency generator has one job: start fast. What does SOLAS demand?

scenes.label: SOLAS II-1/43
scenes.heading: Emergency services supplied within
scenes.narration: Under SOLAS Chapter II-1, the emergency source must connect automatically to the emergency switchboard and supply the required services within 45 seconds.

scenes.label: SOLAS II-1/44
scenes.heading: Starting arrangements
scenes.narration: It must start from cold condition at 0 degrees Celsius. Its starting device needs stored energy for at least three consecutive starts, and a second source must give three more starts within 30 minutes.

scenes.label: WHAT THE ENGINEER CHECKS
scenes.heading: Ready before the blackout
scenes.narration: Batteries or air receiver charged. Emergency fuel tank level checked. Control left in auto. Test the automatic start as your planned maintenance requires.

scenes.label: KEY TAKEAWAY
scenes.heading: Left in manual, it fails when needed
scenes.narration: An emergency generator left in manual is no emergency generator at all.

meta.description: How the emergency generator must start under SOLAS Chapter II-1: automatic connection within 45 seconds, cold start at 0 °C, three consecutive starts and three more from a second source within 30 minutes. Plus what the engineer checks so it works on the day of a blackout.
meta.question: How is the emergency generator started on your ship: battery, hydraulic or air?
